proofs.proof_tex:
By the definition of \(K_G\), it is a nonnegative integer.  Consequently,
\[
K_G\leq 0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad K_G=0.
\]
Apply \(\mathrm{thm:few\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}parent\mbox{-}fixed\mbox{-}parameter\mbox{-}hardness}\) with the fixed parameter value \(k=0\).  Its first assertion says that pointwise numerical edge identification on the promise class \(K_G\leq 0\) is promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete.  By the displayed equivalence and \(\mathrm{def:promise\mbox{-}problem}\), this class is exactly
\[
\mathcal R_0
=
\bigl\{(G,\Sigma,e)\text{ in the promise domain of }\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_3:K_G=0\bigr\}.
\]
Thus the restriction of \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_3\) to \(K_G=0\) is promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete, which proves both the literal \(k=0\) assertion and the more precise completeness assertion.

For the algorithmic consequence, suppose that the residual-algebra construction named by \(\mathrm{def:parameterized\mbox{-}handle}\) yielded an exact algorithm for the stated class with running time \(f(k)\operatorname{poly}(n)\).  On every input in \(\mathcal R_0\), this running time is
\[
f(K_G)\operatorname{poly}(n)=f(0)\operatorname{poly}(n).
\]
If \(N\) is the total binary length of the encoded input, then \(n\leq N\), so the displayed running time is bounded by \(f(0)\operatorname{poly}(N)\).  It is therefore an instance, at \(k=0\), of the \(f(k)\operatorname{poly}(N)\) algorithm ruled out by the complexity consequence in \(\mathrm{thm:few\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}parent\mbox{-}fixed\mbox{-}parameter\mbox{-}hardness}\) unless \(\mathsf P=\forall\mathbb R\).  Contrapositively, unless this equality holds, \(\mathsf{ParamHandle}\) cannot yield such an \(f(k)\operatorname{poly}(n)\) algorithm.

Finally, \(\mathrm{thm:few\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}parent\mbox{-}fixed\mbox{-}parameter\mbox{-}hardness}\) states that its completeness result is obtained by singularity-preserving bijections of the complete coefficient fibers and requires no genericity assumption.  Specializing its construction to \(k=0\) changes neither property.  Therefore the present conclusion includes singular fibers and uses no genericity assumption, as claimed.
